nodes.title: [Bug]: SIGSEGV in MenuBar::RefreshColorCache when creating a framed BrowserWindow with a menu on Wayland (GTK not loaded)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.5.1 (also 46.0.0-nightly.20260929) ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version AlmaLinux 8.10 (RHEL 8 family), GNOME Shell / mutter 3.32.2 on Wayland, GTK 3.22.30, glibc 2.28, x64 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version 38.1.2 ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior A framed `BrowserWindow` with the default application menu opens on a Wayland session. ### Actual Behavior The main process crashes with SIGSEGV inside `new BrowserWindow()`. No window opens. This looks related to #49244, but it is a different call site. #54365 fixed the title bar path. This crash is in the menu bar path, and it still happens on `46.0.0-nightly.20260929`, which includes #54365. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information **Repro** `package.json`: ```json { "name": "repro", "version": "1.0.0", "main": "main.js" } ``` `main.js`: ```js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron') app.whenReady().then(() => { const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 600 }) win.loadURL('data:text/html,

hello

') console.log('window created, electron', process.versions.electron) setTimeout(() => app.quit(), 3000) }) ``` Run from a GNOME Wayland session (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`): `npx electron .` **Results** | Case | Result | |---|---| | 37.10.3, 38.0.0, 38.1.0, 38.1.1, 38.1.2 | OK | | 38.2.0, 38.4.0, 38.8.6, 39.8.10, 40.10.6, 41.10.6, 42.11.10, 44.5.1, 46.0.0-nightly.20260929 | SIGSEGV | | 44.5.1 with `--ozone-platform=x11` or `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11` | OK | | 44.5.1 with `Menu.setApplicationMenu(null)` | OK | | 44.5.1 with `frame: false` | OK | | 44.5.1 with `--gtk-version=3` | SIGSEGV | | 44.5.1 with `app.commandLine.appendSwitch('ozone-platform', 'x11')` in `main.js` | SIGSEGV (switch is applied too late) | 38.1.2 and 38.2.0 use the same Chromium (140.0.7339.133). The only Linux change in 38.2.0 is #48309 ("set ozone platform for wayland"), which made Electron honor `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`. Before 38.2.0 the app ran on X11 on this machine. A framed window without a menu works. A frameless window works (no menu bar is created). The crash needs both a native frame and a menu bar. **Stack trace (44.5.1)** gdb on RHEL 8 (8.2) cannot read the zstd-compressed sections in `electron.debug`, so frames were resolved from its `.symtab` by scanning the crashed thread's stack for return addresses. Frame #0 is a call to address `0x0`. ``` #0 0x0000000000000000 #1 gtk::GtkCheckVersion(unsigned int, unsigned int, unsigned int)+0xb1 #2 gtk::AppendCssNodeToStyleContext(gtk::GtkCssContext, std::string const&)+0x58e #3 gtk::GetStyleContextFromCss(std::string const&)+0x77 #4 gtk::GetBgColor(std::string const&)+0x1a #5 electron::MenuBar::RefreshColorCache(ui::NativeTheme const*)+0x32 #6 electron::MenuBar::MenuBar(electron::NativeWindow*, electron::RootView*)+0x145 #7 electron::RootView::SetMenu(electron::ElectronMenuModel*)+0x65 #8 electron::api::BaseWindow::SetMenu(v8::Isolate*, v8::Local)+0x94 ... electron::api::BaseWindow::InitWith(v8::Isolate*, v8::Local)+0x18 electron::api::BrowserWindow::BrowserWindow(gin::Arguments*, gin_helper::Dictionary const&)+0x35c electron::api::BrowserWindow::New(gin_helper::ErrorThrower, gin::Arguments*)+0xc2 ``` `GtkCheckVersion+0xb1` returns from a call to the `gtk_get_major_version` stub, and the stub jumps through `gtk_get_major_version_ptr`, which is still null. So the GTK symbols were never loaded on this path, but `MenuBar::RefreshColorCache` calls into GTK anyway. The only GTK message in the log before the crash is: ``` ERROR:ui/gtk/gtk_ui.cc:265] Schema org.gnome.desktop.interface does not have key font-antialiasing ``` (The schema on this system is from gsettings-desktop-schemas 3.32. Adding the key removes the message but not the crash.) **Suggested fix** Guard the GTK color lookup in `MenuBar::RefreshColorCache` the same way #54365 guarded the frame view: skip the `gtk::GetBgColor` path, or fall back to `ui::NativeTheme` colors, when GTK is not loaded or no `ui::LinuxUiTheme` is available.

nodes.title: GPU process crashes when offscreen useSharedTexture paints are imported with sharedTexture (Linux, Vulkan)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.4.5 (also seen on 43.1.1) ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version Arch Linux, kernel 6.18 LTS, KDE Plasma 6 (Wayland), Mesa 26.2.2 (RADV) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown. I haven't found a version where it works. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No. It needs Electron's offscreen `useSharedTexture` paints and the `sharedTexture` module, which Chrome doesn't have. ### Expected Behavior An app that takes the `paint` textures of an offscreen window (`offscreen: { useSharedTexture: true }`), imports them with `sharedTexture.importSharedTexture()` and sends them to a normal window with `sharedTexture.sendSharedTexture()` should keep running. ### Actual Behavior With Vulkan enabled (`--use-angle=vulkan --enable-features=Vulkan,VulkanFromANGLE`), the GPU process crashes, usually within the first minute. `child-process-gone` fires with `type: 'GPU'`, reason `crashed`, exit code 133. Chromium restarts it and it keeps crashing. After a few rounds the whole app exits with: ``` FATAL:content/browser/gpu/gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:417] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye. ``` In the gist the receiving page does nothing with the frames except close them, so it isn't about how they're drawn. Without the import step (same offscreen windows, paints released straight away) I haven't seen it crash at all, including one run of over 57,000 paints. Without Vulkan it doesn't crash either. In 4 runs of the gist on 44.4.5, the first GPU crash came at 8.9 s, 28.7 s and 46.1 s, and one run got through 120 s without crashing. GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/ake-app/a298dabf82c35a617c88df23dc1f1ad4 ### Additional Information The gist runs four producer/viewer pairs at 1080p and 120 fps so it crashes sooner. It still happens at 24 fps with one pair, just less often.
In-depth investigation

The first crash in each run is a `CHECK` in `gpu::AddCleanupTaskForSkiaFlush` (`gpu/command_buffer/service/skia_utils.cc:303`, `CHECK_EQ(flush_info->fFinishedProc, &CleanupAfterSkiaFlush)`). Minidump from 44.4.5, symbolized with the release's breakpad symbols: ``` gpu::AddCleanupTaskForSkiaFlush(base::OnceCallback, GrFlushInfo*) gpu::VulkanFenceHelper::CreateExternalCallback() gpu::AddVulkanCleanupTaskForSkiaFlush(viz::VulkanContextProvider*, GrFlushInfo*) viz::SkiaOutputSurfaceImplOnGpu::FlushSurface(...) viz::ReadbackContextTexture::OnMailboxReady(void*) viz::SkiaOutputSurfaceImplOnGpu::RenderSurface(...) viz::SkiaOutputSurfaceImplOnGpu::CopyOutputRGBAInTexture(...) viz::SkiaOutputSurfaceImplOnGpu::CopyOutputRGBA(...) ``` After a restart, some of the later GPU crashes are a different CHECK in `viz::GmbVideoFramePoolContext::InitializeOnGpu`, called from `viz::GpuServiceImpl::GetContextState()`. That looks like a follow-on from the first crash, not a separate bug. How I read the first one: the offscreen `useSharedTexture` paint goes through `CopyOutputRGBAInTexture`, which hands `ReadbackContextTexture::OnMailboxReady` to `FlushSurface` as the flush's finished proc. `FlushSurface` then calls `AddVulkanCleanupTaskForSkiaFlush`. If the Vulkan fence helper has cleanup queued at that moment, `CreateExternalCallback()` returns a task, and `AddCleanupTaskForSkiaFlush` hits the CHECK because the finished proc is already the readback's rather than `CleanupAfterSkiaFlush`. The imported shared textures are what queue that cleanup (for example `SkiaVkOzoneImageRepresentation` end-access and destruction, and `ExternalSemaphorePool`). That's why the readback alone doesn't crash and the import is the trigger. The NV12 readback path has the same shape, so changing `sharedTexturePixelFormat` doesn't help. As far as I can tell, Chromium `main` still has the same code in both functions. Possible fixes: `FlushSurface` could chain the caller's finished proc through the cleanup context, or `CopyOutputRGBAInTexture` could register its readback context via `AddCleanupTaskForSkiaFlush` instead of setting `fFinishedProc` directly. Things I tried that didn't avoid it: `ForceEnableWebGpuInterop` with ANGLE on Vulkan or GL, drawing the frames through WebGPU (`copyExternalImageToTexture` or `importExternalTexture`) or WebGL instead of just closing them, and `supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport`. Turning Vulkan off avoids it, but on this machine that also drops WebGPU to SwiftShader.

nodes.title: Windows: Electron apps crash at launch (exit_code=-2147483645) when Indirect Display Driver adapters are present
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.0.0, 43.6.0, 41.0.3 (three separate apps, all affected) ### What operating system(s) are you using? Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 Home (Chinese), 10.0.26200 (build 26200) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown — the machine has had two Indirect Display Driver (IDD) adapters installed for a long time. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? Yes ### Expected Behavior Electron apps should launch on a Windows machine whose display topology contains **Indirect Display Driver (IDD) adapters** — the virtual monitors used by remote-desktop, screen-streaming, and Android-emulator software. These adapters are a normal, permanent part of many Windows setups (remote work, VDI, streaming, emulators) and are usually the *only* way a remote user can see the screen at all. Electron should either pick the real hardware adapter, or fall back to software rendering. It should not terminate the whole browser process. ### Actual Behavior Three unrelated Electron apps crash on launch, with no window and no error dialog. All three produce the identical fatal sequence: ``` ERROR:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:1108] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645 WARNING:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:1558] The GPU process has crashed 1 time(s) ... (repeats) WARNING:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:1558] The GPU process has crashed 6 time(s) FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:416] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye. ``` `exit_code=-2147483645` is `0x80000003` (`STATUS_BREAKPOINT`). After 6 attempts the app exits immediately. **Affected apps on this machine (all reproducible, all with a clean profile):** | App | Electron | Chrome | Result | |---|---|---|---| | Kimi Desktop | 43.6.0 | 150.0.7871.250 | 0 processes, exits after 6 GPU crashes | | ZCode | 41.0.3 | 146.0.7680.80 | exits after 6 GPU crashes | | DeepSeek Harness | 44.0.0 | 152.0.7977.54 | exits after 6 GPU crashes | Because three different Electron majors (41 / 43 / 44) fail identically, this is **not** a version regression — it is a persistent condition of this machine's display topology. **The only way to launch any of them is `--no-sandbox`**, which works 3/3 times on all three apps. Every other GPU-related flag fails: | Flag | ZCode | DeepSeek Harness | |---|---|---| | `--no-sandbox` | 3/3 works | 3/3 works | | `--disable-gpu-sandbox` | 0/3 | 0/3 | | `--disable-gpu` | 0/3 | 0/3 | | `--disable-gpu-compositing` | 0/3 | 0/3 | | `--use-angle=d3d11` / `d3d11on12` / `gl` / `swiftshader` | 0/3 | 0/3 | | `--in-process-gpu` | 0/3 | 0/3 | `--no-sandbox` is not an acceptable fix for end users: it disables the renderer sandbox and is not something an end user can set on a packaged app anyway. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information #### This is not the DACL / zombie-SID bug I am aware of #51761, #52098, #52255 and #51770. Those are caused by orphaned `S-1-15-2-*` ACEs in the app directory's DACL, and are fixed by `icacls /reset` on the install folder. **That fix does nothing here.** I verified: - The install directories (`D:\software\Kimi`, `D:\software\ZCode`, `D:\software\DeepSeek Harness`) contain **no orphaned or unresolvable SIDs**. - `icacls` reports no "Unknown Account" entries in any of the three install trees. - The crash is 100% reproducible and 100% deterministic; it is not intermittent. - The identical failure occurs on apps installed under `D:\software\` (not `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`), so the MSIX/AppX ACE-leak scenario does not apply. - The failing process is the **GPU process**, and it fails *after* successfully creating at least one adapter — meaning the sandbox launched, but the GPU init inside it did not survive. #### Machine hardware - **CPU:** Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 5 125H (14 cores / 18 threads, Meteor Lake) - **iGPU:** Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics — `PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_7D55&SUBSYS_3E7219E5&REV_08`, driver `31.0.101.5382` - **Display adapters present (`Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController`):** | # | Name | PNP Device ID | Driver | |---|---|---|---| | 0 | `wjIddDriver Device` | `ROOT\DISPLAY\0000` | 9.22.56.244 | | 1 | `Intel(R) Arc(TM) Graphics` | `PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_7D55...` | 31.0.101.5382 | | 2 | `GameViewer Virtual Display Adapter` | `ROOT\DISPLAY\0001` | 15.6.5.199 | Note that **both IDD adapters enumerate before the real Intel adapter** in the Display device class, and they are enumerated on `ROOT\DISPLAY\*` rather than on the PCI bus. #### Why the display topology matters Both non-hardware adapters are genuine Microsoft **Indirect Display Drivers (IDD)** built on the UMDF / `IddCx` framework. From `GameViewerIddDriver.inf` (shipped by the streaming app): ```ini Class = Display ClassGUID = {4D36E968-E325-11CE-BFC1-08002BE10318} [Standard.NTamd64.10.0...22000] %DeviceName%=MyDevice_Install_WIN11, Root\GameViewerIddDriver ; ROOT bus, not PCI [MyDevice_HardwareDeviceSettings] HKR,, "UpperFilters", %REG_MULTI_SZ%, "IndirectKmd" ; <- Microsoft IDD upper filter HKR, "WUDF", "DeviceGroupId", %REG_SZ%, "IddDriverGroup" [MyDevice_Install.NT.Wdf] UmdfService=GameViewerIddDriver,IddDriver_Install UmdfExtensions = IddCx0102 ; <- IddCx indirect display framework ``` These adapters are **dynamic and hot-pluggable**: the kernel PnP log shows the `ROOT\DISPLAY\0000` node being created, torn down and re-created by user-mode software: ``` System log, Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-PnP: [09/28/2026 22:31:08] ID=225 Application \Device\HarddiskVolume4\software\leidian\wujie\bin\wujie.exe (PID 25212) "stopped to remove or eject device" ROOT\DISPLAY\0000 [09/28/2026 18:34:34] ID=219 Driver \Driver\WUDFRd failed to load. Device: ROOT\DISPLAY\0000 status: 0xC0000365 ``` So these display devices appear, disappear and fail to re-initialize while the session is live. An Electron app launching during or after such a transition sees an unstable adapter list. #### Why I believe the GPU process dies rather than falling back The `LOG(FATAL)` in `gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc` is only reached once `FallBackToNextGpuMode()` reports that the fallback stack is exhausted. On Windows `GpuProcessHost::GetFallbackCrashLimit()` is a hard-coded 3, and the stack is `HARDWARE → DISPLAY_COMPOSITOR → SOFTWARE_GL`. Here the GPU process dies 6 times before the fatal, i.e. **it crashes again after every single fallback, including the software path**. That points at something that is not "the hardware adapter is bad", but "the GPU-side sandbox/init cannot complete in this display environment at all". `--no-sandbox` working while `--disable-gpu-sandbox` does not is also informative: `--disable-gpu-sandbox` leaves the GPU process running with the *renderer* sandbox settings (`kNoSandbox` vs `kDisableGpuSandbox` are distinct switches in `sandbox/policy/switches.cc`). The fact that the app comes up only when the whole sandbox is off suggests the failure happens during GPU-process startup, before or outside the GPU sandbox is even the deciding factor.
In-depth investigation

**Adapter enumeration has no IDD / software filter.** `CollectDriverInfoD3D()` in `gpu/config/gpu_info_collector_win.cc` walks DXGI adapters with a plain loop and assigns the first one as the primary GPU: ```cpp for (i = 0; SUCCEEDED(dxgi_factory->EnumAdapters(i, &dxgi_adapter)); i++) { DXGI_ADAPTER_DESC desc; CHECK_EQ(S_OK, dxgi_adapter->GetDesc(&desc)); GPUInfo::GPUDevice device; device.vendor_id = desc.VendorId; device.device_id = desc.DeviceId; // ... if (i == 0) { gpu_info->gpu = device; } else { gpu_info->secondary_gpus.push_back(device); } } ``` There is no check of `DXGI_ADAPTER_FLAG_SOFTWARE`, no check of `D3DKMT_ADAPTERTYPE.IndirectDisplayDevice`, and no preference for PCI-attached adapters. Whatever DXGI returns at index 0 becomes `gpu_info->gpu`. On this machine index 0 (by Display-class enumeration order) is an IDD on the ROOT bus. Chromium is aware that non-PCI display devices exist — bug [973695](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=973695) ("InitializeAndStartSandbox uses the wrong information to lookup devices in fallback databases") was specifically about *"Scenarios such as Windows Virtual Desktop, Remote Desktop and VM connection are not PCI displays"* being mis-parsed. That issue fixed the *parsing* of the device id string, but the enumeration still has no IDD/software classification step. On the ANGLE side the same gap exists: `third_party/angle/src/gpu_info_util/SystemInfo_win.cpp` also enumerates DXGI adapters without filtering IDD devices. **Environment note (why this is a real-world blocker, not an exotic config).** This machine is being controlled remotely. The IDD adapters are the remote-session display: disabling them costs the user control of the machine entirely. Asking the user to uninstall the IDD drivers to make Electron launch is not a workaround — it is a data-loss / lock-out risk. This is the reason such setups are common and will become more common, and it is the reason the fallback chain needs to survive an unexpected adapter rather than kill the browser. **Steps to reproduce the crash on this machine (no special tooling required):** 1. Install any of the three apps above on a machine that has at least one IDD adapter on the ROOT bus. 2. Launch the app with **no** command-line flags. 3. Observe: no window appears; the process exits within ~1 second; running from a shell with `--enable-logging=stderr` prints the six `exit_code=-2147483645` lines followed by `GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.` 4. Relaunch with `--no-sandbox` → the app starts normally. **What a fix could look like (for discussion, not a demand):** 1. When selecting the primary GPU in `CollectDriverInfoD3D()`, skip adapters flagged `DXGI_ADAPTER_FLAG_SOFTWARE` and adapters whose PnP device is on the ROOT bus / whose `D3DKMT_ADAPTERTYPE.IndirectDisplayDevice` bit is set, unless no other adapter exists. 2. Make the GPU fallback chain resilient: if every mode including software rendering is exhausted, prefer to start with GPU disabled (and log loudly) over terminating the browser process. Users strongly prefer a degraded window over no window. 3. At minimum, surface the real reason. `GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.` gives users nothing actionable; the actual GPU-init failure is swallowed before the `LOG(FATAL)`.

nodes.title: Electron on Linux Wayland SIGTRAP on logout | teardown race condition
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

2026.04.1

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

no  idea

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron should tolerate graphical-session teardown and terminate cleanly when the desktop session ends.
Loss of the Wayland/X11 connection or GPU/display resources during logout should not cause the browser process to terminate via SIGTRAP or generate a crash report.

### Actual Behavior

During GNOME logout, the Chromium GPU process can become unusable while Electron is still shutting down.
This eventually and randomly results in a fatal Chromium condition and SIGTRAP, causing crash reporting systems such as Ubuntu Apport to treat an otherwise normal session logout as an application crash.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Example Signal Apport metadata:
```
ProblemType: Crash
Date: Mon Sep 28 11:37:39 2026
ExecutablePath: /opt/Signal Beta/signal-desktop-beta
Package: signal-desktop-beta 8.29.0~beta.1
ProcCmdline: /opt/Signal\ Beta/signal-desktop-beta
Signal: 5
SignalName: SIGTRAP

```
At the same timestamp GNOME begins tearing down the graphical session.
Electron/Chromium processes then report GPU failures with:
```
GPU process exited unexpectedly
GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

The parent Electron process subsequently terminates with SIGTRAP.
The applications work normally again after the next login, so this does not appear to be a persistent GPU initialization failure.

Suspected race
The GNOME graphical session is managed by the systemd user manager.
During logout, application scopes/services and graphical-session components are stopped concurrently. This appears to allow Mutter/GNOME Shell, Wayland/XWayland, or related graphical resources to begin disappearing while Electron's Chromium GPU process is still shutting down.

A suspected sequence is:
1. GNOME logout begins
2. Electron application receives termination and graphical session teardown begins (race starts)
3. Wayland/XWayland/GPU resources disappear before electron teardown
4. Chromium process fails
5. fatal CHECK / SIGTRAP

This would explain why the application behaves normally during normal use but randomly produce a crash report during logout.
Not entirely sure who to blame here, you or the mutter team, but its a fact that non-electron apps (and chromium based browsers) do not cause crashes, so I suspect this is in your court and that your teardown needs some TLC.

For people who are looking for a temp solution, I made a workaround to add a 3 sec delay before wayland itself starts tearing down. The fact that workaround works is one more proof its a race condition. 
You can find it here: [Linux: GNOME logout causes sing-box for Desktop to exit with SIGTRAP and generate core dumps](https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box/issues/4441#issuecomment-5886141278)

nodes.title: Keep menu item images visible when building against the macOS 27 SDK
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

While checking our app against macOS 27, I came across this in Apple's release notes: Apps built against the macOS 27 SDK get every image they put on a menu item hidden, symbol images and regular ones alike, unless they also set the new `preferredImageVisibility` on the `NSMenuItem`. With the 26 SDK, only symbol images are hidden.

Electron is still on the 26 SDK, so current releases are fine. But once it switches, every `icon` set on a `MenuItem` would disappear on macOS 27, and apps couldn't do anything about it. For some apps that's more than a cosmetic problem. The tray menu I'm working on, for example, shows each meeting's start time and color as the item's icon.

Chromium just fixed this for its own menus by setting `preferredImageVisibility` wherever it assigns a menu item image ([crrev.com/c/8463164](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8463164)). Electron's menus don't go through that code though, because `ElectronMenuController` sets `item.image` itself.

I haven't been able to try this myself, since there's no Electron build on the 27 SDK yet.

### Proposed Solution

Do the same as Chromium and set `preferredImageVisibility` to visible wherever Electron sets a menu item image. If an app sets an `icon`, it wants it shown, so I'd just keep the current behavior.

As far as I can tell, that's three places in `electron_menu_controller.mm`: `makeMenuItemForIndex:`, `applyStateToMenuItem:` and `menuItemForService:`. Chromium's new `ui/base/cocoa/macos27_sdk.h` already declares the property for builds against the 26 SDK.

### Alternatives Considered

- Exposing `preferredImageVisibility` as a `MenuItem` option instead: Existing apps would lose their icons on macOS 27 until they opt in. It could still be useful later as an override
- Leaving AppKit's default in place: Apps would silently lose icons they set on purpose

### Additional Information

- Apple's release notes (AppKit section, 170477566 and 179374305): https://developer.apple.com/documentation/macos-release-notes/macos-27-release-notes
- Chromium's [switch to the macOS 27 SDK](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8406027) has already landed and been reverted three times in September, so this might come up soon

nodes.title: [Feature Request]: Docs: `navigateOnDragDrop` opens the dropped URL through `setWindowOpenHandler` (new window), it does not navigate the page
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Problem Description `docs/api/structures/web-preferences.md` describes `navigateOnDragDrop` as "Whether dragging and dropping a file or link onto the page causes a navigation. Default is `false`." That is not what happens. With `navigateOnDragDrop: true`, a link dropped on a page that does not handle the drop is opened as a **new foreground tab request**: `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` is called with `{ url: , disposition: 'foreground-tab', … }`, and without a handler a new `BrowserWindow` is created (`did-create-window` fires). The page that received the drop never navigates: `will-navigate`, `did-start-navigation` and `did-navigate` do not fire and `webContents.getURL()` is unchanged. With the default `false`, the drop is rejected (the page sees a trailing `dragleave`) and nothing opens. Observed on Electron 44.4.5 (Chromium 152.0.7977.130) and 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Chromium 155.0.8046.0), Ubuntu 24.04 x64 under Xvfb, driving the drop with `webContents.debugger` `Input.dispatchDragEvent` (`text/uri-list` item): ``` navigateOnDragDrop: true, with setWindowOpenHandler [+ 1137ms] PAGE DOM dragover types=["text/uri-list"] [+ 1138ms] EVENT setWindowOpenHandler url= http://127.0.0.1:42601/b disposition= foreground-tab -> deny [+ 4291ms] RESULT url now = http://127.0.0.1:42601/a | windows = 1 navigateOnDragDrop: true, no setWindowOpenHandler [+ 1102ms] EVENT app web-contents-created type= window [+ 1106ms] EVENT did-create-window [+ 4261ms] RESULT url now = http://127.0.0.1:44297/a | windows = 2 navigateOnDragDrop: false (default) [+ 1095ms] PAGE DOM dragover types=["text/uri-list"] [+ 1096ms] PAGE DOM dragleave types=["text/uri-list"] [+ 4250ms] RESULT url now = http://127.0.0.1:40137/a | windows = 1 ``` Developers who enable the option because of its name and description expect the page to navigate; instead a window appears (or their `setWindowOpenHandler` is invoked with a URL they did not anticipate). Developers who want the dropped link to load in the same page have to recognise these drops in `setWindowOpenHandler` and call `loadURL` themselves, and nothing in the docs tells them so. ### Proposed Solution Correct the description in `web-preferences.md` (and the mirrored text in `browser-window.md` if present), for example: > `navigateOnDragDrop` boolean (optional) - Whether a file or link dropped onto the page, when the page does not handle the drop itself, is opened by Electron. Default is `false`. When `true`, the dropped URL is opened as a new foreground-tab request: `webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` is called with `disposition: 'foreground-tab'` (a new `BrowserWindow` is created if no handler is set). The page that received the drop is not navigated; to load the URL in the same page, handle it in `setWindowOpenHandler` and call `webContents.loadURL`. ### Alternatives Considered - Changing the behaviour so that `navigateOnDragDrop: true` navigates the receiving page. Chromium deliberately opens dropped URLs in a new tab to avoid data loss in the current tab (crbug.com/451659); Electron only sets `RendererPreferences::can_accept_load_drops` from this option and receives the result as a generic new-tab open request, so a same-page navigation would need Electron-specific plumbing. A docs correction is the low-cost fix. - Leaving the docs as they are: the option's name keeps suggesting a same-page navigation that never happens. ### Additional Information Minimal repro (`main.js`, `package.json` `{"main":"main.js"}`; run `electron . on`, `electron . off`, `electron . on nohandler`). It serves two pages from a local http server and drives the drop through `webContents.debugger` (`Input.dispatchDragEvent`), which enters the same `RenderWidgetHostImpl::DragTargetDrop` path as a platform drop. ```js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron') const http = require('http') const navOn = process.argv.includes('on') const t0 = Date.now() const log = (...a) => console.log(`[+${String(Date.now() - t0).padStart(5)}ms]`, ...a) const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)) const pageA = `A

page A

` app.whenReady().then(async () => { const server = http.createServer((req, res) => { res.setHeader('content-type', 'text/html') res.end(req.url.startsWith('/b') ? '

page B

' : pageA) }) await new Promise((r) => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', r)) const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}` log('navigateOnDragDrop =', navOn) app.on('browser-window-created', () => log('EVENT app browser-window-created')) const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 600, webPreferences: { navigateOnDragDrop: navOn } }) const wc = win.webContents if (!process.argv.includes('nohandler')) { wc.setWindowOpenHandler((d) => { log('EVENT setWindowOpenHandler url=', d.url, 'disposition=', d.disposition, '-> deny'); return { action: 'deny' } }) } wc.on('console-message', (e) => { if (e.message.startsWith('DOM ')) log('PAGE', e.message) }) wc.on('will-navigate', (_e, url) => log('EVENT will-navigate', url)) wc.on('did-navigate', (_e, url) => log('EVENT did-navigate', url)) wc.on('did-create-window', () => log('EVENT did-create-window')) await wc.loadURL(`${base}/a`) await sleep(500) wc.debugger.attach('1.3') const data = { items: [{ mimeType: 'text/uri-list', data: `${base}/b` }], dragOperationsMask: 19 } for (const type of ['dragEnter', 'dragOver', 'dragOver', 'drop']) { await wc.debugger.sendCommand('Input.dispatchDragEvent', { type, x: 300, y: 300, data }) log('CDP Input.dispatchDragEvent', type) await sleep(150) } await sleep(3000) log('RESULT url now =', wc.getURL(), '| windows =', BrowserWindow.getAllWindows().length) process.exit(0) }) ``` Where this comes from: Blink `DragController::PerformDrop` loads a dropped URL that the document did not consume with `NavigationPolicy::kNavigationPolicyNewForegroundTab` ("Open the dropped URL in a new tab to avoid potential data-loss in the current tab. See https://crbug.com/451659"), gated by `ChromeClient::AcceptsLoadDrops()`, which Electron feeds from `navigateOnDragDrop` via `RendererPreferences::can_accept_load_drops` (`shell/browser/web_contents_preferences.cc`). The resulting `NEW_FOREGROUND_TAB` open request reaches Electron's `WebContents::OpenURLFromTab` and is routed to `setWindowOpenHandler` like any other new-window request. This has been Chromium's behaviour since well before Electron's currently supported lines (the same code is at Chromium tags 90 and 100). Found while building Zenium, an Electron-based browser: https://github.com/BenItBuhner/Zenium Prepared with AI assistance (Claude, via Cursor): the investigation and write-up were AI-assisted; the output above was produced by running the code as shown.

nodes.title: [Feature Request]: A way to map a service worker (`ServiceWorkerInfo.renderProcessId`) to its process in `app.getAppMetrics()`
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

We show per-process CPU and memory (a task-manager view) in an Electron browser. For renderers that host a WebContents this works: `webContents.getOSProcessId()` joins with `ProcessMetric.pid` from `app.getAppMetrics()`. For MV3 extension background service workers there is no WebContents, and the APIs that describe the worker cannot be joined with the process list:

- `session.serviceWorkers.getAllRunning()` / `ServiceWorkerInfo` gives `renderProcessId`, which is the render-process-host id (the `webContents.getProcessId()` space), not an OS pid.
- `ProcessMetric` carries only the OS `pid`; renderer rows are `type: 'Tab'` with no `name`.
- `ServiceWorkerMain` has `isDestroyed()`, `send()`, `startTask()`, `ipc`, `scope`, `scriptURL`, `versionId` — nothing about its process.

So a worker-only extension shows up in `getAppMetrics()` as an anonymous `Tab` renderer and its CPU/memory cannot be attributed to the extension. Observed on 44.4.5 and 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Linux x64); the 45.0.0-alpha.11 typings and the current docs (`process-metric.md`, `service-worker-info.md`, `service-worker-main.md`) have no field that would join them.

### Proposed Solution

Any one of these would do:

1. Add the render-process-host id to `ProcessMetric` (e.g. `processId?: number` for renderer rows), so `metric.processId === info.renderProcessId` (and `=== webContents.getProcessId()`), which joins all renderers generically.
2. Expose the OS pid on the worker side: `ServiceWorkerInfo.osProcessId` and/or `ServiceWorkerMain.getOSProcessId()`, mirroring `webContents.getOSProcessId()`.
3. Optionally, fill `ProcessMetric.name` for extension service worker renderers with the extension name, as Chrome's task manager does.

Option 1 is the smallest change; the browser side has both ids on the `RenderProcessHost`.

### Alternatives Considered

- Join through a WebContents of the extension (`chrome-extension://<id>/` origin) that shares the worker's process: fails for worker-only extensions, which have no WebContents unless a popup/options page happens to be open, and the worker is not guaranteed to share that process.
- Elimination (renderer pids in `getAppMetrics()` not owned by any WebContents): only says "some non-WebContents renderer", and is ambiguous as soon as two workers or a spare renderer exist.
- A `service-worker` preload script sending `process.pid` to the main process: with the sandbox on the worker sees `process.pid === 1` on Linux (sandbox pid namespace), not the OS pid; without the sandbox the service-worker preload does not run; and it requires instrumenting every worker in the session.

### Additional Information

`main.js` (`electron main.js`; `extension/manifest.json` contains only `"background": { "service_worker": "sw.js" }`, `sw.js` is `setInterval(() => {}, 1000)`):

```js
const { app, session, webContents } = require('electron')
const path = require('path')

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  const ses = session.defaultSession
  await ses.extensions.loadExtension(path.join(__dirname, 'extension'))
  await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 2000))

  const running = ses.serviceWorkers.getAllRunning()
  console.log('getAllRunning():', JSON.stringify(running))
  const worker = ses.serviceWorkers.getWorkerFromVersionID(Number(Object.keys(running)[0]))
  console.log('ServiceWorkerMain members:', Object.getOwnPropertyNames(Object.getPrototypeOf(worker)).filter(k => !k.startsWith('_') && k !== 'constructor').join(', '))

  const metrics = app.getAppMetrics()
  console.log('ProcessMetric keys:', Object.keys(metrics[0]).join(', '))
  for (const m of metrics) console.log('  ', JSON.stringify({ pid: m.pid, type: m.type, name: m.name, serviceName: m.serviceName }))
  const known = webContents.getAllWebContents().map(wc => wc.getOSProcessId())
  console.log('renderer pids with no WebContents (one of them is the worker):', metrics.filter(m => m.type === 'Tab' && !known.includes(m.pid)).map(m => m.pid))
  app.quit()
})
```

`extension/manifest.json`:

```json
{ "manifest_version": 3, "name": "worker-only-extension", "version": "1.0", "background": { "service_worker": "sw.js" } }
```

Output, Electron 44.4.5 (Chromium 152.0.7977.130), Ubuntu 24.04.4, X11 under Xvfb, x64:

```
getAllRunning(): {"0":{"scriptUrl":"chrome-extension://bcjinncndifnhepabjbbbjonoccihogh/sw.js","scope":"chrome-extension://bcjinncndifnhepabjbbbjonoccihogh/","renderProcessId":5}}
ServiceWorkerMain members: isDestroyed, versionId, scope, scriptURL, ipc, send, startTask
ProcessMetric keys: cpu, pid, type, creationTime, memory
   {"pid":34338,"type":"Browser"}
   {"pid":34369,"type":"GPU","serviceName":"GPU"}
   {"pid":34371,"type":"Utility","name":"Network Service","serviceName":"network.mojom.NetworkService"}
   {"pid":34400,"type":"Tab"}
renderer pids with no WebContents (one of them is the worker): [ 34400 ]
```

`renderProcessId` is `5`; no `ProcessMetric` has `pid === 5`, and nothing on the `Tab` row says which extension it belongs to. 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Chromium 155.0.8046.0) gives the same shape. See also #28114 (more per-process metrics).

nodes.title: macOS: a `WebContentsView` that is in no window reports `isFocused()` true once it loads, and `webContents.getFocusedWebContents()` returns it instead of the window's focused document
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.3.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? macOS ### Operating System Version macOS 14 (GitHub Actions `macos-14`, arm64) and macOS 13 (`macos-13`, x64) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior A `WebContentsView` that has not been added to any window cannot hold a window's keyboard focus. `view.webContents.isFocused()` should be `false` for it, and `webContents.getFocusedWebContents()` should return the WebContents that actually has focus (the window's own `webContents`, whose document reports `document.hasFocus() === true`). ### Actual Behavior On macOS, a `new WebContentsView()` that is never added to a window (created to preload a page, attached to a window later) emits `focus` about a second after `loadURL()` and never `blur`. From then on two WebContents claim focus at once: | what | value | | --- | --- | | `win.webContents.isFocused()` | `true` | | `detached.webContents.isFocused()` | `true` (never goes back to `false`) | | `webContents.getFocusedWebContents().id` | the detached view | | `win.contentView.children` | one hidden view, `isFocused()` `false` | | in the window's document: `document.hasFocus()` / `activeElement` | `true` / the focused `` | So `getFocusedWebContents()` answers with a view that is on no screen while the window's document holds the keyboard. Any main-process code that uses `getFocusedWebContents()` to decide where the keyboard is (menu roles, shortcuts, "which page is active") picks the wrong one. Observed on Electron 44.3.0 (Chromium 152) on macOS 14 arm64 and macOS 13 x64 (GitHub Actions runners, app packaged with electron-builder). Not reproducible on Linux (X11): with 44.4.5 and 45.0.0-alpha.11 the detached view never emits `focus`, `isFocused()` stays `false` and `getFocusedWebContents()` stays the window's webContents. We could not yet re-run on macOS with 44.4.5. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information `main.js` (run with `electron main.js`): ```js const { app, BrowserWindow, WebContentsView, webContents } = require('electron') const t0 = Date.now() const log = (...a) => console.log(`[${Date.now() - t0} ms]`, ...a) const wire = (wc, name) => { wc.on('focus', () => log(`${name} focus`)); wc.on('blur', () => log(`${name} blur`)) } async function snapshot (win, detached, label) { const doc = await win.webContents.executeJavaScript('JSON.stringify({ activeElement: document.activeElement.id, hasFocus: document.hasFocus() })') log(label, `getFocusedWebContents() = ${webContents.getFocusedWebContents()?.id}; win.webContents.isFocused() = ${win.webContents.isFocused()}; detached.isFocused() = ${detached.webContents.isFocused()}; window document ${doc}; win.contentView.children = ${win.contentView.children.length}`) } app.whenReady().then(async () => { const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 600 }) wire(win.webContents, 'window (1)') await win.loadURL('data:text/html,') win.focus(); win.webContents.focus() await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1000)) const detached = new WebContentsView() // never added to any window wire(detached.webContents, 'detached (2)') await snapshot(win, detached, 'before load:') detached.webContents.loadURL('data:text/html,

detached page

') await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 2000)) await snapshot(win, detached, 'after 2 s:') app.quit() }) ``` macOS 14 / 13, Electron 44.3.0 (observed in our app with the same instrumentation): `detached (2) focus` about 1 s after `loadURL`, no `blur`; snapshot as in the table above (`getFocusedWebContents() = 2`, both `isFocused()` true, window document `hasFocus: true`). Linux X11 (Xvfb), Electron 44.4.5 and 45.0.0-alpha.11, same script: no `focus` event for the detached view; `getFocusedWebContents() = 1`, `detached.isFocused() = false` before and after the load.
In-depth investigation

`WebContents::IsFocused()` in `shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents_mac.mm` only consults the key window when the view's NSView has one: ``` auto window = [web_contents()->GetNativeView().GetNativeNSView() window]; if (window && ![window isKeyWindow]) return false; return view->HasFocus(); ``` For a view in no window `window` is `nil`, so the key-window check is skipped and the answer is `RenderWidgetHostViewMac::HasFocus()`, i.e. the view's own first-responder flag, which once set is never resigned for a view that is in no window (there is no window whose first responder could change). The non-Mac implementation checks `GetToplevelWindow()` visibility instead and does not show the problem. `webContents.getFocusedWebContents()` (`lib/browser/api/web-contents.ts`) returns the first WebContents from `getAllWebContents()` whose `isFocused()` is true, so the detached view can be preferred over the window's actually focused document. Presumed fix: in `IsFocused()` return `false` when the NSView has no window (a view in no window cannot be focused), or resign the first-responder state when the view is detached.

Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 24.04.4 (X11, Xvfb 1600x1000, scale factor 1) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior After `view.setBorderRadius(10)` the `WebContentsView` is drawn as a rounded rectangle, with the window background showing in the four corner cutouts. When DevTools is opened docked in that view (`view.webContents.openDevTools({ mode: 'bottom' })`), the page and the toolbox share the same box, so we expect the box to keep its four rounded outer corners and the page's two corners at the page/toolbox seam to be square, with no gap between page and toolbox. ### Actual Behavior With DevTools docked, only the page is rounded: - the two outer corners now occupied by the toolbox (bottom-left / bottom-right for `mode: 'bottom'`) are square: the DevTools frontend paints right up to the corner pixel; - the two outer corners still occupied by the page are rounded, but the cutout shows the DevTools frontend's white background instead of the window background; - the page's two corners at the seam are rounded as well, leaving a white notch of the corner radius at each end of the seam. `setBorderRadius(0)` makes everything square and the seam whole; closing DevTools brings the rounded box back. Same with `mode: 'right'`, same when `setBorderRadius()` is called after DevTools is already open, same with and without `--disable-gpu`, same on 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Chromium 155.0.8046.0). ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information `main.js` (run with `electron main.js`; it reads the pixels back through `desktopCapturer`, so the window must be on an unobscured display — we used `xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1600x1000x24" electron --disable-gpu main.js`; the effect is also visible by eye): ```js const { app, BrowserWindow, WebContentsView, desktopCapturer, screen } = require('electron') const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)) app.whenReady().then(async () => { console.log('versions:', process.versions.electron, process.versions.chrome) console.log('legend: window background #eeeeee = rgb(238,238,238); page #e8f0fe = rgb(232,240,254); DevTools frontend = white / near-white') const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 1200, height: 800, backgroundColor: '#eeeeee' }) const view = new WebContentsView() win.contentView.addChildView(view) view.setBounds({ x: 40, y: 40, width: 1120, height: 720 }) view.setBorderRadius(10) await view.webContents.loadURL('data:text/html,') await sleep(1500) // Reads screen pixels with desktopCapturer; d = distance along the diagonal from the corner. async function report (label, devtoolsOpen) { const { width, height } = screen.getPrimaryDisplay().size const [src] = await desktopCapturer.getSources({ types: ['screen'], thumbnailSize: { width, height } }) const bmp = src.thumbnail.toBitmap() // BGRA const w = src.thumbnail.getSize().width const rgb = (x, y) => { const i = (y * w + x) * 4; return `rgb(${bmp[i + 2]},${bmp[i + 1]},${bmp[i]})` } const cb = win.getContentBounds() const x0 = cb.x + 40; const y0 = cb.y + 40; const x1 = x0 + 1119; const y1 = y0 + 719 const corners = { 'view top-left': (d) => [x0 + d, y0 + d], 'view top-right': (d) => [x1 - d, y0 + d], 'view bottom-left': of the docked toolbox let seam = y1 + 1 for (let y = y0 + 12; y <= y1; y++) if (rgb(x0 + 12, y) !== 'rgb(232,240,254)') { seam = y; break } seamInfo = `, page/toolbox seam at y=${seam}` corners['page bottom-left (seam)'] = (d) => [x0 + d, seam - 1 - d] corners['page bottom-right (seam)'] = (d) => [x1 - d, seam - 1 - d] } console.log(`[${label}] view on screen x=${x0}..${x1} y=${y0}..${y1}${seamInfo}`) for (const [name, at] of Object.entries(corners)) { console.log(` ${name.padEnd(25)}`, [0, 1, 2, 3].map((d) => `d=${d} ${rgb(...at(d))}`).join(' | ')) } } await report('radius 10, no DevTools', false) const opened = new Promise((r) => view.webContents.once('devtools-opened', r)) view.webContents.openDevTools({ mode: 'bottom', activate: true }) await opened await sleep(2500) await report('radius 10, DevTools docked bottom', true) view.setBorderRadius(0) await sleep(1000) await report('radius 0, DevTools docked bottom', true) app.quit() }) ``` Output on Electron 44.4.5 (`d` = pixels along the diagonal from the corner into the view; a radius-10 corner reads "colour behind the view" at `d=0..2` and the page at `d=3`): ``` versions: 44.4.5 152.0.7977.130 legend: window background #eeeeee = rgb(238,238,238); page #e8f0fe = rgb(232,240,254); DevTools frontend = white / near-white [radius 10, no DevTools] view on screen x=240..1359 y=169..888 view top-left d=0 rgb(238,238,238) | d=1 rgb(238,238,238) | d=2 rgb(238,238,238) | d=3 rgb(232,240,254) view top-right d=0 rgb(238,238,238) | d=1 rgb(238,238,238) | d=2 rgb(238,238,238) | rgb(238,238,238) | d=3 rgb(232,240,254) [radius 10, DevTools docked bottom] view on screen x=240..1359 y=169..888, page/toolbox seam at y=589 view top-left d=0 rgb(255,255,255) | d=1 rgb(255,255,255) | d=2 rgb(255,255,255) | d=3 rgb(232,240,254) view top-right d=0 rgb(255,255,255) | d=1 rgb(255,255,255) | d=2 rgb(255,255,255) | d=3 rgb(232,240,254) view bottom-left d=0 rgb(255,255,255) | d=1 rgb(255,255,255) | d=2 rgb(255,255,255) | d=3 rgb(255,255,255) view bottom-right d=0 rgb(252,252,252) | d=1 rgb(252,252,252) | d=2 rgb(252,252,252) | d=3 rgb(252,252,252) page bottom-left (seam) d=0 rgb(255,255,255) | d=1 rgb(255,255,255) | d=2 rgb(255,255,255) | d=3 rgb(232,240,254) page bottom-right (seam) d=0 rgb(255,255,255) | d=1 rgb(255,255,255) | d=2 rgb(255,255,255) | d=3 rgb(232,240,254) [radius 0, DevTools docked bottom] view on screen x=240..1359 y=169..888, page/toolbox seam at y=589 view top-left d=0 rgb(232,240,254) | d=1 rgb(232,240,254) | d=2 rgb(232,240,254) | d=3 rgb(232,240,254) view top-right d=0 rgb(232,240,254) | d=1 rgb(232,240,254) | d=2 rgb(232,240,254) | d=3 rgb(232,240,254) view bottom-left d=0 rgb(255,255,255) | d=1 rgb(255,255,255) | d=2 rgb(255,255,255) | d=3 rgb(255,255,255) view bottom-right d=0 rgb(252,252,252) | d=1 rgb(252,252,252) | d=2 rgb(252,252,252) | d=3 rgb(252,252,252) page bottom-left (seam) d=0 rgb(232,240,254) | d=1 rgb(232,240,254) | d=2 rgb(232,240,254) | d=3 rgb(232,240,254) page bottom-right (seam) d=0 rgb(232,240,254) | d=1 rgb(232,240,254) | d=2 rgb(232,240,254) | d=3 rgb(232,240,254) ``` Reading the tables: without DevTools every corner is window background ×3 then page, i.e. the box is rounded. With DevTools docked at the bottom, the view's top corners are DevTools white ×3 then page (the page is still rounded, but over an unclipped DevTools surface instead of the window), the bottom corners are white / `rgb(252,252,252)` all the way in (the toolbox is square), and the page's corners at the seam are white ×3 then page (the notch). With radius 0 the seam corners are page colour all the way and nothing is rounded. `mode: 'right'` gives the mirror image on the right-hand corners (page/toolbox seam at x=805 in the same geometry); 45.0.0-alpha.11 gives identical tables.
In-depth investigation

`WebContentsView::SetBorderRadius()` (`shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents_view.cc`) calls `View::SetBorderRadius()` and then `ApplyBorderRadius()`, which hands the radius to `InspectableWebContentsView::SetCornerRadii()` (`shell/browser/ui/inspectable_web_contents_view.cc`): ```cpp void InspectableWebContentsView::SetCornerRadii( const gfx::RoundedCornersF& corner_radii) { // WebView won't exist for offscreen rendering. if (contents_web_view_) { contents_web_view_->holder()->SetNativeViewCornerRadii(corner_radii); // ... SetIsFastRoundedCorner(false) on the native view's layer (Aura) } } ``` The radii only reach the native-view host of `contents_web_view_`, the page. When DevTools is docked, `InspectableWebContentsView::Layout()` runs `ApplyDevToolsContentsResizingStrategy()` and gives `devtools_web_view_` the whole container while the page is laid out in the inset the frontend asks for: ```cpp devtools_web_view_->SetBoundsRect(new_devtools_bounds); SetContentsViewBounds(new_contents_bounds); ``` `devtools_web_view_->holder()` never receives corner radii, and the clip path that `View::ApplyBorderRadius()` sets on the container does not clip the layer-backed `WebView`s. So the DevTools surface is a square covering the whole view and the page surface is rounded on all four of its own corners, two of which are now at the seam: the page's arcs reveal the DevTools surface beneath (white in the cutouts of the outer corners, the notches at the seam), and the toolbox's corners are never clipped. The function is identical on `main`, and it has behaved this way since `setBorderRadius()` was added in 33.0.0 (#42320, at the time `contents_web_view_->holder()->SetCornerRadii(...)`), so there is no last-known-good version. A fix without API changes: have `SetCornerRadii()` remember the radii and apply them to `devtools_web_view_->holder()` as well (with the same `SetIsFastRoundedCorner(false)` treatment), and in `Layout()` — when DevTools is docked — give each host only the corners that coincide with the container's corners, e.g. for `mode: 'bottom'` `gfx::RoundedCornersF(r, r, 0, 0)` for the page and `gfx::RoundedCornersF(0, 0, r, r)` for the toolbox (for `right`: page `(r, 0, 0, r)`, toolbox `(0, r, r, 0)`), restoring all four corners on the page when DevTools is closed or undocked. `gfx::RoundedCornersF` already supports per-corner values.

Related: #51342 (per-corner radii in `setBorderRadius`) would let an app zero the two seam corners itself, but the docked toolbox would still be square. nodes.title: `webContents.print({ silent: true, pageRanges })` prints every page on Linux; the ranges are dropped from silent print jobs
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.4.5 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 24.04.4 (X11, Xvfb; CUPS 2.4.7 with a cups-pdf queue) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior `webContents.print({ silent: true, deviceName, pageRanges: [{ from: 1, to: 1 }] })` on a three-page document should print one page (the second), the way `webContents.printToPDF({ pageRanges: '2' })` renders one page and the way `lp -o page-ranges=2` prints one page on the same CUPS queue. ### Actual Behavior All three pages are printed, for every range we tried (`[{ from: 1, to: 1 }]`, `[{ from: 0, to: 0 }]`, `[{ from: 0, to: 1 }]`). The callback reports `success = true` with no `failureReason`. The CUPS job is submitted as a three-page PDF (`job-impressions-completed = 3`) and carries no `page-ranges` attribute, so nothing downstream can restore the selection. `printToPDF` with the equivalent range in the same process produces one page. Same result on 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Chromium 155.0.8046.0). Reported before in #25013 (Windows, closed by #25064, which fixed the system-dialog paths on macOS/Windows); a 2024 comment there reports the same on Ubuntu with 30/31. The open refactor #53083 rewrites this code path. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information Setup (Ubuntu 24.04): `sudo apt-get install -y cups printer-driver-cups-pdf poppler-utils cups-ipp-utils && sudo service cups start && sudo lpadmin -p PDF -E -v cups-pdf:/ -m lsb/usr/cups-pdf/CUPS-PDF_opt.ppd && sudo lpadmin -d PDF` (output files land in `~/PDF/`). `main.js` (run with `electron main.js`; set `PRINTER=` if the target queue is not the default): ```js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron') const fs = require('fs') const path = require('path') // 0-based, inclusive: [{ from: 1, to: 1 }] = page 2 only (override with PAGE_RANGES='[{"from":0,"to":0}]') const pageRanges = JSON.parse(process.env.PAGE_RANGES || '[{"from":1,"to":1}]') const html = `pageRanges repro
Page one
Page two
Page three
` app.whenReady().then(async () => { console.log('versions:', process.versions.electron, process.versions.chrome, process.versions.node) const win = new BrowserWindow({ show: false }) await win.loadURL('data:text/html;charset=utf-8,' + encodeURIComponent(html)) // control: printToPDF with the equivalent (1-based) range fs.writeFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'control.pdf'), await win.webContents.printToPDF({ pageRanges: '2' })) const printers = await win.webContents.getPrintersAsync() const deviceName = process.env.PRINTER || printers.find((p) => p.isDefault)?.name || printers[0].name const options = { silent: true, deviceName, pageRanges, printBackground: true } console.log('print options:', JSON.stringify(options)) win.webContents.print(options, (success, failureReason) => { console.log('print callback:', success, failureReason || '') setTimeout(() => app.quit(), 3000) }) }) ``` Observed, Electron 44.4.5 (`xvfb-run -a electron main.js`, then `pdfinfo`, `lpstat`, `ipptool`): ``` versions: 44.4.5 152.0.7977.130 24.21.0 print options: {"silent":true,"deviceName":"PDF","pageRanges":[{"from":1,"to":1}],"printBackground":true} print callback: true control.pdf: Pages: 1 <- printToPDF({ pageRanges: '2' }) lpstat -W completed -o: PDF-9 ubuntu 8192 Thu 24 Sep 2026 09:32:39 PM UTC spool output: ~/PDF/pageRanges_repro-job_9.pdf -> Pages: 3 <- webContents.print(...) ipptool -tv ipp://localhost/jobs/9 get-job-attributes.test: copies (integer) = 1 document-format (mimeMediaType) = application/pdf number-up (integer) = 1 job-impressions-completed (integer) = 3 job-media-sheets-completed (integer) = 3 (no page-ranges attribute) ``` `PAGE_RANGES='[{"from":0,"to":0}]'` and `'[{"from":0,"to":1}]'` give the same 3-page output. The three spool pages are distinct pages 1–3 (checked with `pdftoppm`). Control on the same queue: `lp -d PDF -o page-ranges=2 ~/PDF/pageRanges_repro-job_9.pdf` → 1 page, `page-ranges (rangeOfInteger) = 2-2`, `job-impressions-completed = 1`. 45.0.0-alpha.11: identical results for all three ranges.
In-depth investigation

The ranges are converted and delivered correctly up to the renderer, then discarded by the silent branch: 1. `WebContents::Print` (`shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.cc`) turns `pageRanges: [{ from, to }]` into the 1-based `printing::kSettingPageRange` list in the job settings dictionary. 2. In the renderer, Electron's `patches/chromium/printing.patch` makes `PrintRenderFrameHelper::Print()` call `InitPrintSettings(frame, node, settings)`, which sends the dictionary to the browser over the Electron-only sync `UpdatePrintSettings` IPC. The browser side, `PrintViewManagerElectron::CompleteGetPrintPreviewParams` (`shell/browser/printing/print_view_manager_electron.cc`), replies with a `PrintPagesParams` whose `pages` is `printing::GetPageRangesFromJobSettings(job_settings)`, i.e. the requested ranges; `InitPrintSettings` stores it with `SetPrintPagesParamsForPrinting(*settings)`, so at this point `print_pages_params_->pages` holds the ranges. 3. Back in `Print()`, the patch replaces the dialog step with: ```cpp if (silent) { print_settings = mojom::PrintPagesParams::New(); print_settings->params = print_pages_params_->params->Clone(); } else { print_settings = GetPrintSettingsFromUser( frame_ref.GetFrame(), node, expected_page_count, print_request_type); } ... SetPrintPagesParamsForPrinting(*print_settings); ``` The new `PrintPagesParams` copies only `params`; its `pages` vector is empty, and `SetPrintPagesParamsForPrinting` overwrites the stored params with it. 4. `PrintRenderFrameHelper::OnFramePreparedForPrintPages` (`components/printing/renderer/print_render_frame_helper.cc`) computes `PageNumber::GetPages(print_pages_params_->pages, page_count)`; an empty range list means "all pages", so all pages are rendered and spooled (as a single PDF on Linux, which is why CUPS never sees a `page-ranges` attribute either). In the non-silent branch `GetPrintSettingsFromUser` → browser `OnDidScriptedPrint` sets `params->pages = printer_query->settings().ranges()`, which is why the dialog path was fixable in #25064 without touching this code. A one-line fix for the silent branch is `print_settings->pages = print_pages_params_->pages;` (or `std::move`) before `SetPrintPagesParamsForPrinting`. #53083 removes this branch altogether and sets `params->pages` from the job's ranges in the browser, which should also fix it.

nodes.title: Refusing a request in `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler` rejects `getDisplayMedia()` with `AbortError: Invalid capture constraints` instead of `NotAllowedError`
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.4.5 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 24.04.4 (X11, Xvfb) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior When the `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler` handler declines a request (the user closed the app's source picker without choosing, or the app does not allow screen sharing for that page), the page's `navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia()` promise should reject with `NotAllowedError`, which is what a page gets when the user cancels the picker in Chrome, and what Electron itself produces when the request is refused one step earlier in `setPermissionRequestHandler` (`callback(false)` → `NotAllowedError: Permission denied`). There should be one documented way to decline from the handler that does not throw in the main process. ### Actual Behavior Every way of declining from the display-media handler rejects the page's promise with `AbortError: Invalid capture constraints`. Two of them also throw a `TypeError` synchronously inside the handler (an unhandled exception unless the app wraps the `callback` call). `getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true })` from a user gesture, Electron 44.4.5: | Handler action | Main process | Page: `err.name: err.message` | | --- | --- | --- | | `setDisplayMediaRequestHandler` → `callback(null)` | – | `AbortError: Invalid capture constraints` | | … → `callback(undefined)` | – | `AbortError: Invalid capture constraints` | | … → `callback()` | – | `AbortError: Invalid capture constraints` | | … → `callback({})` | `TypeError: Video was requested, but no video stream was provided` | `AbortError: Invalid capture constraints` | | … → `callback({ video: undefined })` | `TypeError: video must be a WebFrameMain or DesktopCapturerSource` | `AbortError: Invalid capture constraints` | | `setPermissionRequestHandler` → `callback(false)` (control) | – | `NotAllowedError: Permission denied` | Pages that follow the usual web pattern (`if (err.name === 'NotAllowedError') { /* user cancelled */ } else { /* capture failed */ }`) therefore show a "could not start screen capture" style error for a plain cancellation. Declining in the permission handler instead is not equivalent: in 44 the permission request for `getDisplayMedia()` arrives as `permission: "media"` with `mediaTypes: []`, and in any version the handler has to decide before the app's picker has been shown, so "user cancelled the picker" can only be expressed from the display-media handler. Same result on 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Chromium 155.0.8046.0). The `session.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler` docs describe the `streams` object but not how to decline. See also #47980 (same question, closed without a repro) and #45517 (the `TypeError` for `callback({ video: undefined })`). ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information `main.js` (run with `electron main.js`; the page is served over `http://127.0.0.1` because `navigator.mediaDevices` is not available on `data:` URLs, and the call is made with a user gesture via `executeJavaScript(code, true)`): ```js const { app, BrowserWindow, session } = require('electron') const http = require('http') const shapes = [ { label: 'display-media callback(null)', dm: (cb) => cb(null) }, { label: 'display-media callback(undefined)', dm: (cb) => cb(undefined) }, { label: 'display-media callback()', dm: (cb) => cb() }, { label: 'display-media callback({})', dm: (cb) => cb({}) }, { label: 'display-media callback({ video: undefined })', dm: (cb) => cb({ video: undefined }) }, { label: 'permission-handler callback(false)', permissionDeny: true } ] let current = null app.whenReady().then(async () => { const ses = session.defaultSession ses.setPermissionRequestHandler((wc, permission, callback, details) => { console.log(' permission request:', JSON.stringify({ permission, mediaTypes: details.mediaTypes })) callback(!(current && current.permissionDeny)) }) ses.setDisplayMediaRequestHandler((request, callback) => { console.log(' display-media request:', JSON.stringify({ video: request.videoRequested, audio: request.audioRequested, userGesture: request.userGesture })) try { current.dm(callback) } catch (e) { console.log(' handler callback threw:', e.message) } }) const server = http.createServer((req, res) => { res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/html'); res.end('

getDisplayMedia repro

') }) await new Promise((r) => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', r)) const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 600 }) await win.loadURL(`http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}/`) for (const shape of shapes) { current = shape console.log(`--- getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true }) with ${shape.label} ---`) console.log(' page:', await win.webContents.executeJavaScript( `navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true }).then(s => 'RESOLVED', e => 'REJECTED ' + e.name + ': ' + e.message)`, true)) } app.quit() }) ``` Output, Electron 44.4.5, `xvfb-run -a electron main.js` (Linux X11): ``` --- getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true }) with display-media callback(null) --- permission request: {"permission":"media","mediaTypes":[]} display-media request: {"video":true,"audio":true,"userGesture":true} page: REJECTED AbortError: Invalid capture constraints --- getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true }) with display-media callback(undefined) --- permission request: {"permission":"media","mediaTypes":[]} display-media request: {"video":true,"audio":true,"userGesture":true} page: REJECTED AbortError: Invalid capture constraints --- getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true }) with display-media callback() --- permission request: {"permission":"media","mediaTypes":[]} display-media request: {"video":true,"audio":true,"userGesture":true} page: REJECTED AbortError: Invalid capture constraints --- getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true }) with display-media callback({}) --- permission request: {"permission":"media","mediaTypes":[]} display-media request: {"video":true,"audio":true,"userGesture":true} handler callback threw: Video was requested, but no video stream was provided page: REJECTED AbortError: Invalid capture constraints --- getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true }) with display-media callback({ video: undefined }) --- permission request: {"permission":"media","mediaTypes":[]} display-media request: {"video":true,"audio":true,"userGesture":true} handler callback threw: video must be a WebFrameMain or DesktopCapturerSource page: REJECTED AbortError: Invalid capture constraints --- getDisplayMedia({ video: true, audio: true }) with permission-handler callback(false) --- permission request: {"permission":"media","mediaTypes":[]} page: REJECTED NotAllowedError: Permission denied ``` On 45.0.0-alpha.11 the permission request line reads `{"permission":"display-capture","mediaTypes":["audio","video"]}` (#52824); the page results are unchanged.
In-depth investigation

`ElectronBrowserContext::DisplayMediaDeviceChosen` (`shell/browser/electron_browser_context.cc`) runs the `content::MediaResponseCallback` with `blink::mojom::MediaStreamRequestResult::INVALID_DISPLAY_CAPTURE_CONSTRAINTS` in every refusal case: when the handler's result `IsNullOrUndefined()`, when it is not an object, when `video` is neither a `WebFrameMain` nor a `DesktopCapturerSource` (`ThrowTypeError("video must be a WebFrameMain or DesktopCapturerSource")`), and when video was requested but none was provided (`ThrowTypeError("Video was requested, but no video stream was provided")`). Blink maps that result code to `DOMExceptionCode::kAbortError` (`third_party/blink/renderer/modules/mediastream/user_media_request.cc`, the `INVALID_DISPLAY_CAPTURE_CONSTRAINTS` / `INVALID_GUM_*_CAPTURE_CONSTRAINTS` cases) with the message `"Invalid capture constraints"` (`ErrorCodeToString` in `user_media_processor.cc`). The permission-handler path goes through `MediaAccessAllowed(request, callback, /*allowed=*/false)` in `shell/browser/web_contents_permission_helper.cc`, which runs the callback with `MediaStreamRequestResult::PERMISSION_DENIED`; Blink maps `PERMISSION_DENIED` / `PERMISSION_DISMISSED` / `PERMISSION_DENIED_BY_USER` to `kNotAllowedError` ("Permission denied" / "Permission denied by user"). A small fix would be to treat a null/undefined result from the display-media handler as the user's refusal and run the callback with `PERMISSION_DENIED_BY_USER` (or `PERMISSION_DISMISSED`) instead of `INVALID_DISPLAY_CAPTURE_CONSTRAINTS`, and to document `callback(null)` as the way to decline; the `TypeError` cases can stay `INVALID_DISPLAY_CAPTURE_CONSTRAINTS` since they are programming errors.
