nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.4.5 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 24.04 (X11, Xvfb) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior After `Security.enable` succeeds on a `webContents.debugger` session, the session receives `Security.visibleSecurityStateChanged` (the current state immediately, then on every change), as the DevTools protocol documents and as Chrome delivers it. Alternatively, `Security.enable` fails, or the Electron docs state that the Security domain's events are not available over `webContents.debugger`. ### Actual Behavior `Security.enable` resolves with `{}` and no `Security.*` event ever follows: not on enable, not across a reload, not across navigations. The same session receives `Network.*` and `Page.*` events normally, and the document response's `securityDetails` shows the connection is a plain, valid TLS 1.3 connection (`securityState: "secure"`). Output of the repro below on 44.4.5 (page served by a local https server whose certificate is trusted through `setCertificateVerifyProc`; zero `certificate-error` events): ``` [+ 170ms] Security.enable -> {} [+ 3173ms] methods seen 3 s after Security.enable: [] [+ 3174ms] Security.setIgnoreCertificateErrors -> {} [+ 3174ms] Network.enable -> {} [+ 6177ms] Network.responseReceived (Document) after reload: [{"url":"https://localhost:36253/","securityState":"secure","issuer":"localhost","subjectName":"localhost","protocol":"TLS 1.3"}] [+ 6177ms] Security.* methods seen overall: [] [+ 7682ms] Page.* seen after Page.enable + reload: ["Page.frameStartedNavigating","Page.frameStartedLoading","Page.frameNavigated","Page.domContentEventFired","Page.loadEventFired","Page.frameStoppedLoading"] ``` Identical on 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Chromium 155.0.8046.0). Practical effect: a browser-style app cannot get the page's security state (and the certificate issuer for the site-information UI) through the protocol the way it can in Chrome; the `Security` domain looks fully enabled but is silent. Reading `securityDetails` from `Network.responseReceived` or recording certificates in `setCertificateVerifyProc` works as a workaround. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information Minimal repro. Create a self-signed certificate next to `main.js`, then run `electron .` (`package.json`: `{"main":"main.js"}`): ``` openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -subj /CN=localhost -keyout k.pem -out c.pem -days 2 ``` ```js const { app, BrowserWindow, session } = require('electron') const https = require('https') const fs = require('fs') const path = require('path') const t0 = Date.now() const log = (...a) => console.log(`[+${String(Date.now() - t0).padStart(5)}ms]`, ...a) const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms)) app.whenReady().then(async () => { const server = https.createServer( { key: fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'k.pem')), cert: fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, 'c.pem')) }, (req, res) => { res.setHeader('content-type', 'text/html'); res.end('

hello over https

') } ) await new Promise((r) => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', r)) const url = `https://localhost:${server.address().port}/` // Trust the self-signed certificate for this process, so no 'certificate-error' fires. session.defaultSession.setCertificateVerifyProc((_req, cb) => cb(0)) const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 600 }) const wc = win.webContents await wc.loadURL(url) const dbg = wc.debugger dbg.attach('1.3') const seen = [] const docs = [] dbg.on('message', (_e, method, params) => { seen.push(method) if (method === 'Network.responseReceived' && params.type === 'Document') { const sd = params.response.securityDetails || null docs.push({ url: params.response.url, securityState: params.response.securityState, issuer: sd && sd.issuer, protocol: sd && sd.protocol }) } }) log('Security.enable ->', JSON.stringify(await dbg.sendCommand('Security.enable'))) await sleep(3000) log('methods seen 3 s after Security.enable:', JSON.stringify(seen)) log('Security.setIgnoreCertificateErrors ->', JSON.stringify(await dbg.sendCommand('Security.setIgnoreCertificateErrors', { ignore: true }))) log('Network.enable ->', JSON.stringify(await dbg.sendCommand('Network.enable'))) wc.reload() await sleep(3000) log('Network.responseReceived (Document) after reload:', JSON.stringify(docs)) log('Security.* methods seen overall:', JSON.stringify(seen.filter((m) => m.startsWith('Security.')))) log('Page.enable ->', JSON.stringify(await dbg.sendCommand('Page.enable'))) wc.reload() await sleep(1500) log('Page.* seen after Page.enable + reload:', JSON.stringify([...new Set(seen.filter((m) => m.startsWith('Page.')))])) server.close() process.exit(0) }) ``` Environment used: Electron 44.4.5 (Chromium 152.0.7977.130, Node 24.21.0) and 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Chromium 155.0.8046.0), Ubuntu 24.04.4 x64 under Xvfb (X11), Chromium sandbox enabled.
In-depth investigation

Chromium implements the `Security` domain twice: - `content/browser/devtools/protocol/security_handler.cc` (//content) implements the commands (`enable`, `disable`, `setIgnoreCertificateErrors`, `setOverrideCertificateErrors`, `handleCertificateError`) and the `certificateError` event only. Its `Enable()` calls `AttachToRenderFrameHost()`, which calls `DidChangeVisibleSecurityState()` "to send an initial event", but the class does not override that `WebContentsObserver` method (its header lists only `DidFinishNavigation` under "WebContentsObserver overrides"), so the call is a no-op and `frontend_->VisibleSecurityStateChanged` is never reached anywhere in //content. - `chrome/browser/devtools/protocol/security_handler.cc` (//chrome) is the emitter: `Enable()` → `DidChangeVisibleSecurityState()` → `CreateVisibleSecurityState(web_contents())` (built on `SecurityStateTabHelper`) → `frontend_->VisibleSecurityStateChanged(...)`. It is wired through Chrome's `ChromeDevToolsSession`. Electron builds only a few `//chrome/browser/devtools/*` utility files (`chromium_src/BUILD.gn`: contents resizing strategy, embedder message dispatcher, eye dropper, file system indexer, settings, features, visual logging) and nothing from `//chrome/browser/devtools/protocol/`; `shell/browser/ui/devtools_manager_delegate.cc` `HandleCommand()` handles `Browser.close` and forwards everything else to //content. Every DevTools client of an Electron `WebContents` (`webContents.debugger`, `--remote-debugging-port`, the DevTools frontend) therefore gets the //content handler, whose `Security.enable` succeeds while the event that the protocol documents for it does not exist in this build. Options: implement the event in Electron's DevTools layer (a small `WebContentsObserver::DidChangeVisibleSecurityState` bridge that builds `Security.VisibleSecurityState` from `content::WebContents::GetController().GetVisibleEntry()->GetSSL()` — the //chrome version is 289 lines and depends on `SecurityStateTabHelper`, which Electron does not have; a reduced version could report `securityState`, `certificateSecurityState.certificate`/`issuer`/`subjectName`/`protocol`/`validFrom`/`validTo` from `SSLStatus`), or document on `debugger.md` that the Security domain's `visibleSecurityStateChanged` / `securityStateChanged` events are not available and point at `Network.responseReceived.response.securityDetails` and `session.setCertificateVerifyProc` instead. Verified against Chromium `main` sources on 2026-09-24; the behaviour is the same in the Chromium 152 (Electron 44) and 155 (Electron 45 alpha) builds tested.

nodes.title: `webContents` never emits `unresponsive` while `webContents.debugger` is attached
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.4.5 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 24.04 (X11, Xvfb) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior A renderer that stops responding is reported through `webContents.on('unresponsive')` whether or not the app holds a `webContents.debugger` session on that `webContents`. A session that only issues emulation or instrumentation commands (`Emulation.*`, `Network.enable`, …) and is not paused at a breakpoint should not disable the hang report. If the suppression is intended, it should be documented on the `unresponsive` event and on `debugger.attach()`; today neither page mentions it. ### Actual Behavior While any `webContents.debugger` session is attached, `unresponsive` (and the matching `responsive`) is never emitted for that `webContents`. Detaching restores it. With the repro below (a button whose click handler runs `for(;;){}`; the click is sent with `sendInputEvent`): - no debugger attached: `unresponsive` fires 16.0 s after the click; - `debugger.attach('1.3')` plus one `Emulation.setHardwareConcurrencyOverride` command, session left attached: no `unresponsive` within 60 s (`debugger.isAttached()` is `true`); - same attach and command, then `debugger.detach()` before the click: `unresponsive` fires 16.0 s after the click. Output on 44.4.5 (Ubuntu 24.04, Xvfb, sandbox enabled): ``` A: no debugger [+ 636ms] clicked hang button [+ 16644ms] EVENT unresponsive B: debugger attached [+ 132ms] debugger attached; Emulation.setHardwareConcurrencyOverride -> {} [+ 634ms] clicked hang button [+ 60695ms] RESULT variant=B waited=60s after click (no EVENT line) C: attached, then detached before the click [+ 643ms] clicked hang button [+ 16651ms] EVENT unresponsive ``` Same on 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Chromium 155.0.8046.0): A fires at 16.0 s, B never fires within 60 s. Any app that keeps a CDP session on a page for its own purposes (emulation, network instrumentation, throttling) therefore loses hang detection for that page without any indication. The same happens to every page under Playwright for Electron or any `--remote-debugging-port` client with `Target.setAutoAttach`, so hang handling cannot be tested under such a harness. ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information Minimal repro, `main.js` (with `{"main":"main.js"}` in `package.json`). Run `electron . A 45`, `electron . B 60`, `electron . C 45` (A = no debugger, B = attached, C = attached then detached; the number is how many seconds to wait after the click). The renderer is deliberately hung; the process exits by itself after the wait. ```js const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron') const variant = process.argv.find((a) => /^[ABC]$/.test(a)) || 'A' const waitMs = Number(process.argv.find((a) => /^\d+$/.test(a)) || 45) * 1000 const t0 = Date.now() const log = (...args) => console.log(`[+${String(Date.now() - t0).padStart(6)}ms]`, ...args) app.whenReady().then(async () => { log('versions', process.versions.electron, process.versions.chrome) const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 600 }) const wc = win.webContents wc.on('unresponsive', () => log('EVENT unresponsive')) wc.on('responsive', () => log('EVENT responsive')) await wc.loadURL('data:text/html,') if (variant === 'B' || variant === 'C') { wc.debugger.attach('1.3') const r = await wc.debugger.sendCommand('Emulation.setHardwareConcurrencyOverride', { hardwareConcurrency: 2 }) log('debugger attached; Emulation.setHardwareConcurrencyOverride ->', JSON.stringify(r)) } if (variant === 'C') { wc.debugger.detach() log('debugger detached') } log('debugger.isAttached() =', wc.debugger.isAttached()) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500)) wc.sendInputEvent({ type: 'mouseDown', x: 50, y: 50, button: 'left', clickCount: 1 }) wc.sendInputEvent({ type: 'mouseUp', x: 50, y: 50, button: 'left', clickCount: 1 }) log('clicked hang button') setTimeout(() => { log(`RESULT variant=${variant} waited=${waitMs / 1000}s after click (no EVENT line above = never fired)`) process.exit(0) }, waitMs) }) ``` Environment used: Electron 44.4.5 (Chromium 152.0.7977.130, Node 24.21.0) and 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Chromium 155.0.8046.0), Ubuntu 24.04.4 x64 under Xvfb (X11), Chromium sandbox enabled.
In-depth investigation

The gate is applied in Electron's code. `patches/chromium/refactor_unfilter_unresponsive_events.patch` (from #44629) removes Chromium's `ShouldIgnoreUnresponsiveRenderer()` early return from `WebContentsImpl::RendererUnresponsive` so that every hang reaches Electron, and Electron re-applies the same predicate before emitting: - `main`: `shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.cc`, `WebContents::RendererUnresponsive`: `bool should_ignore = web_contents_impl->ShouldIgnoreUnresponsiveRenderer(); … if (!should_ignore && visible && renderer_initialized) EmitWithoutEvent("unresponsive", event_object);` - `44-x-y`: the same three fields are put on the internal `-unresponsive` event and `lib/browser/api/web-contents.ts` emits `unresponsive` only when `!event.shouldIgnore && event.visible && event.rendererInitialized`. `content::WebContentsImpl::ShouldIgnoreUnresponsiveRenderer()` returns `DevToolsAgentHost::IsDebuggerAttached(this)` as its last step, i.e. true for any attached DevTools client of the `WebContents`, with the upstream comment `// TODO(pfeldman): Fix this to only return true if the renderer is *actually* sitting on a breakpoint. https://crbug.com/684202`. `webContents.debugger.attach()` creates such a client, so `shouldIgnore` is true for as long as the session lives. Chrome uses the predicate only to hide its hung-page dialog; in Electron it silently removes the app's only hang signal. Possible directions: emit `unresponsive` regardless of `IsDebuggerAttached` (the visibility and sleep cases were already reworked in #53529, so the predicate is already Electron's decision); or track whether the attached session is actually paused (`Debugger.paused` without a matching `Debugger.resumed`) and ignore only then; or exclude `webContents.debugger` sessions from the check (they belong to the app, not to a developer at a breakpoint). At minimum, document the current behaviour on `unresponsive` and `debugger.attach()`. See also #14257 (2018, the inverse case: `unresponsive` firing while paused in DevTools, which is what the debugger check protects against).

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.4.5 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 24.04.4 (X11, Xvfb) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior A preload script registered with `session.registerPreloadScript({ type: 'service-worker', ... })` runs in the session's extension service workers regardless of whether the app was started with `--no-sandbox`, or the API documents that it requires the sandbox and warns when it is skipped. ### Actual Behavior With the sandbox on, the preload runs in an MV3 extension's background service worker (`process.type === 'service-worker'`, `contextIsolated: true`, `sandboxed: true`) and the global it sets through `contextBridge.executeInMainWorld` is visible to the worker script. With `--no-sandbox` the same preload never runs: the worker starts and runs normally, `chrome.*` is populated, but the global is `undefined`. `session.getPreloadScripts()` reports the registration in both cases and nothing is logged. | Electron | sandbox | worker sees `__preloadRan` | | --- | --- | --- | | 44.4.5 (Chromium 152.0.7977.130) | on | `"type=service-worker contextIsolated=true sandboxed=true"` | | 44.4.5 | `--no-sandbox` | `undefined` | | 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Chromium 155.0.8046.0) | on | `"type=service-worker contextIsolated=true sandboxed=true"` | | 45.0.0-alpha.11 | `--no-sandbox` | `undefined` | ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information Four files; run `electron main.js` and `electron main.js --no-sandbox`. `main.js`: ```js const { app, session } = require('electron') const path = require('path') app.whenReady().then(async () => { console.log('sandbox:', process.argv.includes('--no-sandbox') ? 'off (--no-sandbox)' : 'on') const ses = session.fromPartition('persist:probe') ses.registerPreloadScript({ type: 'service-worker', id: 'diag', filePath: path.join(__dirname, 'worker-preload.js') }) console.log('getPreloadScripts():', JSON.stringify(ses.getPreloadScripts())) ses.serviceWorkers.on('console-message', (_e, d) => console.log(`[service worker console] ${d.message}`)) await ses.extensions.loadExtension(path.join(__dirname, 'extension')) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 3000)) app.quit() }) ``` `worker-preload.js`: ```js const { contextBridge } = require('electron') contextBridge.executeInMainWorld({ func: (info) => { globalThis.__preloadRan = info }, args: [`type=${process.type} contextIsolated=${process.contextIsolated} sandboxed=${process.sandboxed}`] }) ``` `extension/manifest.json`: ```json { "manifest_version": 3, "name": "sw-preload-probe", "version": "1.0", "background": { "service_worker": "sw.js" } } ``` `extension/sw.js`: ```js console.log('__preloadRan=' + JSON.stringify(globalThis.__preloadRan) + ' chrome=' + Object.keys(chrome).sort().join(',')) ``` Output, Electron 44.4.5, `electron main.js`: ``` sandbox: on getPreloadScripts(): [{"filePath":".../worker-preload.js","id":"diag","type":"service-worker"}] [service worker console] __preloadRan="type=service-worker contextIsolated=true sandboxed=true" chrome=dom,extension,i18n,management,runtime,tabs ``` `electron main.js --no-sandbox`: ``` sandbox: off (--no-sandbox) getPreloadScripts(): [{"filePath":".../worker-preload.js","id":"diag","type":"service-worker"}] [service worker console] __preloadRan=undefined chrome=dom,extension,i18n,management,runtime,tabs ``` 45.0.0-alpha.11 behaves the same in both cases. Ubuntu 24.04.4, X11 under Xvfb, x64.
In-depth investigation

`ElectronMainDelegate::CreateContentRendererClient` (`shell/app/electron_main_delegate.cc`) instantiates `ElectronSandboxedRendererClient` when `IsSandboxEnabled(command_line)` is true and `ElectronRendererClient` otherwise; `IsSandboxEnabled` (`shell/app/command_line_args.cc`) is simply `--enable-sandbox` present or `--no-sandbox` absent, so `--no-sandbox` switches every renderer, including service-worker renderers, to `ElectronRendererClient`. Only `ElectronSandboxedRendererClient::WillEvaluateServiceWorkerOnWorkerThread` (`shell/renderer/electron_sandboxed_renderer_client.cc`) creates the preload realm: when `context_proxy->ElectronPreloadData().has_value()` it allocates `ServiceWorkerData` and calls `preload_realm::OnCreatePreloadableV8Context`. `ElectronRendererClient` does not override `WillEvaluateServiceWorkerOnWorkerThread`, so the base `RendererClientBase` implementation runs (`shell/renderer/renderer_client_base.cc`), which only forwards to the extensions dispatcher; the only service-worker reference in `electron_renderer_client.cc` is the `IsServiceWorkerGlobalScope()` bail-out in the Node integration check. The browser side still attaches the preload data (hence `getPreloadScripts()` looks fine), it is just never consumed. Either running the preload realm from `ElectronRendererClient` as well (the realm is sandbox-style, `contextIsolated: true`, and does not need Node in the worker), or documenting in `session.registerPreloadScript` / `--no-sandbox` that `service-worker` preloads require the sandbox and emitting a warning when they are dropped, would resolve this.

nodes.title: Hidden `WebContentsView` (`setVisible(false)`) takes the window's keyboard focus when a navigation commits in it
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.4.5 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 24.04.4 (X11, Xvfb) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior A `WebContentsView` that is hidden (`view.setVisible(false)`) and that the app never called `focus()` on should not become the focused WebContents when a page loads in it. Keyboard focus should stay where it was (here: a focused `` in the window's own `webContents`). Use case: a browser-style app loads background tabs (middle-click, `target=_blank`) into hidden `WebContentsView`s while the user types in the visible one. ### Actual Behavior The moment the hidden view's main-frame navigation commits, the window's `webContents` emits `blur`, the hidden view's `webContents` emits `focus`, `webContents.getFocusedWebContents()` returns the hidden view, `view.webContents.isFocused()` is `true`, and in the visible document `document.hasFocus()` becomes `false`. Focus stays with the hidden view, so subsequent key events go to a widget that is not on screen (in our app, keyboard shortcuts handled by the visible content stop working until focus is moved back). Observed on 44.4.5 (Chromium 152.0.7977.130) and 45.0.0-alpha.11 (Chromium 155.0.8046.0), Linux X11 under Xvfb, sandbox on. `about:blank` does not trigger it; a `data:` or `http:` page does. `webPreferences: { focusOnNavigation: false }` on the hidden view avoids it, but that also disables focus-on-navigation for the view once it is shown; there is no way to keep the default for visible views and skip hidden ones. See also #42339 (option to stop an added view from grabbing focus) and #42578 (fixed by the `focusOnNavigation` opt-out). ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information `main.js` (run with `electron main.js`; add `--focus-on-navigation-false` to try the opt-out): ```js const { app, BrowserWindow, WebContentsView, webContents } = require('electron') const t0 = Date.now() const log = (...a) => console.log(`[${Date.now() - t0} ms]`, ...a) const wire = (wc, name) => { wc.on('focus', () => log(`${name} focus`)); wc.on('blur', () => log(`${name} blur`)) } const snapshot = async (win, label) => log(label, 'focused webContents =', webContents.getFocusedWebContents()?.id, 'chrome document:', await win.webContents.executeJavaScript('JSON.stringify({ activeElement: document.activeElement.id, hasFocus: document.hasFocus() })')) app.whenReady().then(async () => { const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 800, height: 600 }) wire(win.webContents, 'window webContents (1)') await win.loadURL('data:text/html,') win.focus(); win.webContents.focus() await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1000)) await snapshot(win, 'before:') const opts = process.argv.includes('--focus-on-navigation-false') ? { webPreferences: { focusOnNavigation: false } } : {} const view = new WebContentsView(opts) wire(view.webContents, 'hidden view (2)') view.setVisible(false) win.contentView.addChildView(view) view.webContents.loadURL('data:text/html,

background page

') // never shown, never focused by the app await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 1500)) await snapshot(win, 'after 1.5 s:') log('hidden view: getVisible() =', view.getVisible(), 'isFocused() =', view.webContents.isFocused()) app.quit() }) ``` Output, Electron 44.4.5, `xvfb-run -a electron main.js`: ``` [127 ms] window webContents (1) focus [1141 ms] before: focused webContents = 1 chrome document: {"activeElement":"url","hasFocus":true} [1145 ms] window webContents (1) blur [1146 ms] hidden view (2) focus [2648 ms] after 1.5 s: focused webContents = 2 chrome document: {"activeElement":"url","hasFocus":false} [2648 ms] hidden view: getVisible() = false isFocused() = true ``` With `--focus-on-navigation-false`: no `blur`/`focus`, focused webContents stays `1`, `hasFocus: true`. 45.0.0-alpha.11 behaves the same as 44.4.5 in both cases.
In-depth investigation

`WebContents::ReadyToCommitNavigation` in `shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.cc` calls `web_contents()->SetInitialFocus()` for every main-frame commit when the owner window is active, `type_ == Type::kBrowserWindow` (which is the type a `WebContentsView`'s webContents gets) and `WebContentsPreferences::ShouldFocusOnNavigation()` is true. It does not consider whether the `views::View` hosting the WebContents is visible (`WebContentsView.getVisible()` / `views::View::IsDrawn()`), so a hidden child view is focused like a visible one and, on Linux (aura), its hidden widget then holds the focus. A check such as "skip `SetInitialFocus()` when the hosting view is not drawn" would keep the current default for visible views and leave `focusOnNavigation: false` for apps that never want it.

Found while building Zenium, an Electron-based browser: https://github.com/BenItBuhner/Zenium Prepared with AI assistance (Claude, via Cursor): the investigation and write-up were AI-assisted; the repro output above was produced by running the code as shown.

I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior When a WebAuthn request reaches a USB security key that requires a PIN and Electron has no PIN prompt to show, the request should reject (for example with `NotAllowedError`) and the app should keep running. ### Actual Behavior The browser process dies with SIGTRAP from a CHECK about 0.7 s after launch, during `navigator.credentials.create()` and before the key is touched. Results with the gist on 43.4.0: | Keys plugged in | Result | |---|---| | YubiKey 5 only | Crash during `create()`, no touch | | YubiKey 4 only | `create()` OK, `get()` OK | | Both; YubiKey 4 touched | `create()` OK, `get()` OK; the log shows a clean cancel of the YubiKey 5's operation | The YubiKey 5 (USB `1050:0406`, firmware 5.8.0) reports `alwaysUv: true`, `uv: true`, `clientPin: true`, `bioEnroll: true`, `makeCredUvNotRqd: false`, and `pinUvAuthToken: true`, so every operation needs user verification. The YubiKey 4 (USB `1050:0407`) is U2F only. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/nisavid/a7e5438b6ceef5a0761898dc99ec6b64 ### Additional Information The gist is a minimal main-process app that serves `index.html` on `http://localhost` and runs `navigator.credentials.create()` for a non-resident credential with `userVerification: "discouraged"`, then `navigator.credentials.get()` with that credential. `get()` takes `userVerification` from the `uv` query parameter (default `discouraged`); `REPRO_QUERY='?uv=preferred'` sets it, which the crashing runs used, though the single-key run crashed inside `create()` before `get()` ran. Run it with a PIN-protected FIDO2 key plugged in: ``` electron . --enable-logging=stderr --vmodule=device_event_log_impl=1 ``` This is narrower than #24573, which tracks the missing Linux FIDO2 PIN UI: here a request that needs the PIN takes the browser process down instead of rejecting. It surfaced in the Proton Pass desktop app (`/usr/lib/electron43/electron /usr/share/proton-pass/app.asar`), whose in-app sign-in crashed three times on 2026-09-24 with a main-thread stack identical to the gist's. Chrome was not tested.
In-depth investigation

The distro `electron43` binary is stripped. `systemd-coredump` labels frame 0 `cppgc::internal::FatalImpl`, but that 7-byte exported symbol (`push rbp; mov rbp,rsp; int3; ud2`) is an identical-code-folded `IMMEDIATE_CRASH` stub, so the name is a misattribution. Identifying the other frames by the source-path strings their functions reference gives: a `device.mojom.HidConnection` read, then `device/fido/hid/fido_hid_device.cc` (message received), then the `device/fido/ctap2_device_operation.h` response callback, then the crash stub. The gist's core has the same stack hash as the Proton Pass cores. My reading, as inference: the key's `alwaysUv` makes the request need PIN/UV, the request handler moves on to PIN collection after reading the retry counts, and with no PIN UI on Linux the browser process hits a CHECK instead of failing the request.

x64

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

After a secondary display is disconnected and then reconnected, and the app's `BrowserWindow` has moved back onto it, minimizing and then restoring the window should keep it on that same display.

### Actual Behavior

The window restores onto the display it was temporarily forced onto during the disconnect, not the display it was actually on when it was minimized.

Repro:
1. Open the app so its window sits on Screen 2 (a secondary/extended display).
2. Disconnect Screen 2. Windows moves the window to Screen 1 (expected, since its previous location no longer exists).
3. Reconnect Screen 2. Windows moves the window back to Screen 2 (expected).
4. Minimize the window.
5. Restore it (click the taskbar icon).
6. **The window reappears on Screen 1 instead of Screen 2**, even though it was visibly on Screen 2 immediately before being minimized.

This looks like Windows' `WINDOWPLACEMENT.rcNormalPosition` (the rect used to restore a minimized window) isn't refreshed when the OS auto-relocates the window during the temporary disconnect/reconnect in steps 2-3, so restoring from minimize replays the stale placement from step 2 instead of the window's actual, current position.

This has a real privacy/security impact: it's common to use a secondary monitor to present/share content to a remote audience while keeping other windows on a private primary monitor. If an unrelated app (in our case, a communications/IM client) is minimized and restored while that secondary monitor is being shared, it can unexpectedly reappear on the shared screen and expose private content (chat messages, notifications, etc.) to the audience instead of staying on the private display.

Reproduced with a completely default, unmodified `BrowserWindow` (no code touches window position on `minimize`/`restore`/`show`), so this does not appear to be application-specific behavior.

nodes.title: [Bug]: linux-x64 main process dies with SIGTRAP via out-of-range std::string_view::substr (hardened libc++ → LogMessage::HandleFatal → IMMEDIATE_CRASH) — Electron 41.0.3
nodes.body:
### Electron Version

41.0.3 (linux-x64; stock release binary, GNU build ID `bb7c19abf4fef1dba088a8a3595b42c17e188af8`). Current 41.x line is 41.10.7 / Chromium 146.0.7680.216 — unknown whether this is already fixed there.

### Operating System

Arch Linux (Omarchy), kernel 7.2.5 x64, Wayland (Hyprland), AMD Granite Ridge iGPU + mesa 26.2.2. Host: 30GiB RAM, no memory pressure at crash times.

### Last Known Working Electron Version

Unknown — crashes began with an app whose bundled runtime is 41.0.3; we could not A/B other Electron versions.

### What happened

A production Electron app's **main process dies instantly with SIGTRAP (`si_code=SI_KERNEL`)** — no dialog, no JS exception, nothing in the app log. Four occurrences in 5 days on one machine, always while the app was **idle** (internal telemetry seconds before each crash: 0 running tasks, 0 leases, 1 window). Two of the four crashes happened within 4 minutes of each other (relaunch → crash after 3m19s). Not correlated with memory (no OOM, 14GiB free), CPU, or user workload.

### Analysis (symbolicated with the official `electron-v41.0.3-linux-x64-debug.zip`)

All crashes land on the **same instruction**, module-relative vaddr `0x6EDE0E4` of the `electron` binary (verified across two app releases that ship the identical runtime):

```
addr2line -e debug/electron.debug -f -C -i 0x6EDE0E4
  → logging::LogMessage::HandleFatal(...)   ./../../base/immediate_crash.h:180
addr2line -e debug/electron.debug -f -C -i 0x2ae9680
  → std::__Cr::__throw_out_of_range(char const*)   ./../../third_party/libc++/src/include/stdexcept:249
```

The trap block loads the rodata string `"string_view::substr"` and calls `__throw_out_of_range` with it before the `int3` (`IMMEDIATE_CRASH`). Chain: **`std::string_view::substr(pos, …)` called with `pos > size()`** → hardened libc++ assertion (`string_view:470`) → with exceptions disabled, funneled to `logging::LogMessage::HandleFatal` (`base/logging.cc:1009`) → `IMMEDIATE_CRASH()` (`int3`) → SIGTRAP.

I.e., a native `substr` bounds violation anywhere in the main process (Electron/Chromium/Node code or a native module) is fatal by design under Chromium's hardened libc++, and in this case it recurs on a ~daily cadence.

### Timing hint (unconfirmed)

The app performs periodic `git.refresh`-style RPCs; one completed **4.8s** and another **0.24s** before the two most recent traps — a network/hostname-adjacent path is a plausible trigger. The exact caller could not be recovered: `systemd-coredump` stored cores are truncated (~22MB) and lack the crashing thread's stack.

### What I'd like

1. A check whether an out-of-range `string_view::substr` fix landed between Chromium 146.0.7680.**80** and **.216** (or in Electron's own code between 41.0.3 and 41.10.7).
2. Pointers on which main-process subsystems call `string_view::substr` on network/hostname-derived data, if that rings a bell.

Happy to provide: the four coredump records (PIDs, timestamps, truncated cores), app-log excerpts around each crash, trap-block disassembly, and the full symbolication transcript. A reproducible test case is not yet available (caller unidentified); I can re-run capture with a full-core setup if useful.

nodes.title: Linux: app hard-freezes when it fires a notification with no notification daemon (sync libnotify call wedges UI thread)
nodes.body:
# Linux: Electron app hard-freezes when it fires a notification with no notification daemon

> Sync libnotify call wedges the UI thread. App must be SIGKILLed. Sound, GPU,
> and Wayland backend all falsified as causes. Bisected 2026-09-22.

## Environment

- OS: Arch-based (CachyOS), KDE Plasma 6.7.5, Wayland, single 1080p@144 panel
- App: `opencode-desktop` 1.18.32 (AppImage), Electron 42.3.3, native Wayland
  ozone (also reproduced with `--ozone-platform=x11`)
- Same repro on Discord desktop (Electron 42.11.1, native Wayland) — not
  app-specific
- `org.freedesktop.Notifications` ownerless on the session bus (Plasma never
  claims it; reproduced across reboots; 43 activation timeouts across 6 boots
  in retained journals)

## Repro (100% once the bus name is dead)

1. Ensure no notification daemon owns `org.freedesktop.Notifications`
   (verify: `busctl --user list | grep Notifications` shows `(activatable)`,
   no owner).
2. Leave the Electron app unfocused.
3. Trigger any app notification (e.g. task-completion ping, chat mention).
4. Refocus the app window.

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: notification delivered or silently dropped; app responsive.
- Actual: entire window dead — no repaint, no input, close button dead.
  Process alive but fully stalled; kill leaves a compositor ghost until the
  WM "not responding" prompt. Must SIGKILL + relaunch.

## Forensic evidence

- The frozen app logs the cause itself:
  `libnotify_notification.cc:61 notify_notification_show: Error calling
  StartServiceByName for org.freedesktop.Notifications: Timeout was reached`
- Bus-level proof, reproducible by hand:
  `busctl --user call org.freedesktop.Notifications … Notify …` →
  `Call failed: Connection timed out`. Activation spawns `plasma_waitforname`,
  which exits 1 (`Service was not registered within timeout`).
- `gstack` of the frozen renderer (18 threads): all parked in `epoll_wait` /
  `pthread_cond_wait` — no renderer deadlock; the wedge is the browser main
  thread inside the synchronous D-Bus call (browser/GPU procs unattachable
  under sandbox namespaces).
- Bisected out:
  - DSP/audio stack — froze with effects bypassed AND with the audio daemon
    fully killed (zero nodes in `pw-dump`).
  - Ozone backend — froze on both `wayland` and `x11`.
  - GPU — clean `dmesg`, no `i915` errors, compositor healthy, other apps
    unaffected.
- Discriminators: in-app mute does NOT prevent it (the notify call still
  fires); Do-Not-Disturb DOES (no call made). Running any daemon
  (`dunst`/`mako`) eliminates it.

## Upstream refs

- electron/electron#21912 — identical freeze, closed ("run dunst or another
  notification system").
- electron/electron#14006 — names `g_dbus_proxy_call_sync` in
  `libnotify_notification.cc` as the blocker (log shows Discord activating
  `org.freedesktop.Notifications`).
- KDE Discuss (Feb 2026) — Plasma-side refusal to host the name, messaging
  apps hanging for the 60s timeout, event-queue buildup.

## Suggested fix

Make the Linux notify path asynchronous (or time-bound with a short timeout)
so a missing/broken daemon degrades to a dropped notification instead of a
wedged UI thread; alternatively detect no-owner up front and skip the call.

### Electron Version

42-x-y and 43-x-y

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 build 26200.9448

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

V8 should succeed in tiering-up WebAssembly, resulting in boosted performance. This should happen silently in the background, and of course, not crash.

### Actual Behavior

V8 crashes when attempting to tier-up _any_ WASM that includes WASM-based exception handling. Such WASM can be created by compiling via Emscripten with `--fwasm-exceptions`, not `--fexceptions` or no exception handling. To be clear, it's V8's tier-up operation that crashes, not the WebAssembly code.

The crash can appear to happen at random because Electron/V8 — not the code attempting to call the WASM — decides when to tier-up WASM.

Also, I saw this on both Windows and Mac.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Even though it's V8 that's crashing, the bug is in Electron code, not V8.

The upstream commit (written against V8 main, Aug 2026) declares the new
builtin as
`IF_WASM(TFS, WasmGetOwnProperty, NeedsContext{false}, kObject, kSymbol)`
and makes the Turboshaft descriptor `kNeedsContext = false`, passing two
arguments (`exception`, `symbol`) at three call sites in
`turboshaft-graph-interface.cc` (catch tag lookup ×2, exception value
unpacking) and in Liftoff.

On main, `NeedsContext` is `base::StrongAlias<NeedsContextTag, bool>`
(since V8 commit `a59996fbddf`, 2026-07-01), so `NeedsContext{false}` means
"no context". In V8 15.0 (and 14.8) that commit is absent and
`src/common/globals.h:3010` still reads
`enum class NeedsContext { kYes, kNo };`. Brace-initialising that enum from
`false` yields enumerator 0 = **kYes**. The line compiles and silently
inverts: the builtin's interface descriptor keeps a context parameter, so
the call descriptor has 3 parameters (`Descriptor:r1s0i4f0` in
`--trace-turbo-graph`) while every `Call` op only has 2 arguments
(`Call(#callee, #exception, #symbol)`).

In `patches/v8/cherry-pick-36079c36283a.patch` on 43-x-y and 42-x-y, the
`builtins-definitions.h` hunk must use the enum spelling of those branches:
```
-  IF_WASM(TFS, WasmGetOwnProperty, NeedsContext{false}, kObject, kSymbol)
+  IF_WASM(TFS, WasmGetOwnProperty, NeedsContext::kNo, kObject, kSymbol)
```
(or drop the backport on those lines). Electron 44.x and later are not affected.

### Problem Description

Google has just announced Googlebook, a new desktop platform:

https://googlebook.google/

For developers maintaining cross-platform Electron applications, there is currently no clear path for targeting Googlebook as a first-class platform.

As Googlebook is a desktop platform and may become relevant to existing Electron applications, it would be useful to clarify whether Electron intends to support Googlebook, and what form that support might take.

### Proposed Solution

Consider adding Googlebook as an officially supported Electron target platform, if technically feasible.

At this early stage, it would also be helpful to have guidance from the Electron team on whether Googlebook support is being considered, and whether it could be implemented through existing Linux support or would require a separate platform backend.

### Alternatives Considered

One possible alternative is running the existing Linux build of an Electron application through Googlebook's Linux environment, assuming this is supported and provides sufficient desktop integration.

Another option for applications with multiple frontends would be to maintain a separate Android-native or other Googlebook-compatible frontend. However, this would reduce the benefit of using Electron as a cross-platform desktop application framework.

### Additional Information

Googlebook was announced only about 20 minutes ago at the time of filing this issue, so I understand that it is extremely early and that the exact scope or feasibility of Electron support may not yet be known.

Official Googlebook website:

https://googlebook.google/

This issue is primarily intended to start a discussion about compatibility and the Electron project's plans for this new platform.
